citation: Fee Schedule, section 1 (About this schedule)
text:
Fee Schedule > 1. About this schedule

This Fee Schedule lists the fees Rubies Microfinance Bank charges for everyday services. It covers transfers, accounts, cards, alerts, statements and loans. Every fee is shown in naira before you confirm an action. Rubies does not add hidden charges. Where a fee is zero, the service is free. Fees may change; the current version is always the one shown in the app or given by a chat agent. This schedule explains what each fee is for. It does not explain how to dispute a charge; the Disputes and Complaints Procedure explains that.

citation: Fee Schedule, section 2 (Transfer fees)
text:
Fee Schedule > 2. Transfer fees

Rubies transfer fees apply to transfers sent to another bank over the NIP network. A transfer of up to ₦5,000 costs ₦10. A transfer from ₦5,001 to ₦50,000 costs ₦25. A transfer above ₦50,000 costs ₦50 plus ₦3.75 VAT, total ₦53.75. VAT is charged at 7.5% of the fee. A transfer to another Rubies account costs ₦0. The fee is calculated on the amount you send, not on your balance. Rubies shows the fee on screen before you confirm, so you always know the total that will leave your account.

citation: Fee Schedule, section 3 (Account fees)
text:
Fee Schedule > 3. Account fees

Rubies keeps everyday account fees low. A savings account maintenance fee is ₦0, so you are not charged a monthly fee to keep a savings account open. A balance enquiry costs ₦0, whether you check in the app, by USSD, or with a chat agent. A mini statement costs ₦0. These zero fees mean that checking your own money is always free. Other account services, such as a certified statement, have their own fees, which are listed under SMS alerts and statements in this Fee Schedule.

citation: Fee Schedule, section 4 (Card fees)
text:
Fee Schedule > 4. Card fees

Rubies debit card fees cover issuing and replacing your card. Issuing a new debit card costs ₦1,000. Replacing a lost or damaged debit card costs ₦1,500. Blocking a card costs ₦0. When you report a lost card, blocking takes effect immediately after you confirm the action with the chat agent. You will be told clearly that the card is blocked. A replacement card is sent after the replacement fee is paid. Card fees are charged once, at the time of the request.

citation: Fee Schedule, section 5 (SMS alerts and statements)
text:
Fee Schedule > 5. SMS alerts and statements

Rubies charges for SMS alerts and some statements. Each SMS alert costs ₦4. You can receive an alert for every debit and credit on your account. A certified statement costs ₦1,000. A mini statement costs ₦0 and shows your most recent transactions. A balance enquiry costs ₦0. If you do not want SMS alerts, you can turn them off so the ₦4 charge does not apply. Certified statements are usually requested for official purposes such as visa applications or loan applications.

citation: Fee Schedule, section 6 (Loan fees)
text:
Fee Schedule > 6. Loan fees

Rubies loan fees are charged upfront. A management fee of 1% of the loan amount is charged before disbursement. An insurance fee of 0.5% of the loan amount is also charged upfront. Rubies offers two products: the Quick Salary Loan and the Small Business Loan. Loan tenors run from 3 to 12 months. For a ₦200,000 loan, the management fee is ₦2,000 and the insurance fee is ₦1,000, a total upfront cost of ₦3,000. Whether you qualify for a loan depends on eligibility checks, which are explained when you apply.

citation: Fee Schedule, section 7 (Services with no fee)
text:
Fee Schedule > 7. Services with no fee

Several Rubies services carry no fee. Sending money to another Rubies account costs ₦0. Savings account maintenance costs ₦0. A mini statement costs ₦0. A balance enquiry costs ₦0. Blocking a card costs ₦0. These services are free because Rubies wants customers to move and check their own money without extra cost. When a service is free, no charge is added later. If a fee ever applies to a service you are using, the chat agent will tell you the amount before you confirm.

citation: Fee Schedule, section 8 (Disputing a fee)
text:
Fee Schedule > 8. Disputing a fee

If you think a fee is wrong, you can dispute it. Rubies will first propose the dispute and explain what will happen. Nothing is logged until you say yes. Once you agree, Rubies opens a ticket and gives you a ticket number. You then receive an acknowledgement within 24 hours. The full steps, the resolution timelines, and how to escalate are in the Disputes and Complaints Procedure. Keep your transaction reference and the date of the charge ready when you raise the dispute.

citation: Fee Schedule, section 9 (Sources and currency)
text:
Fee Schedule > 9. Sources and currency

Rubies fee figures are set by Rubies Microfinance Bank. The permitted fee types are guided by the CBN Guide to Charges. The CBN Guide to Charges link is to be confirmed. Date read: 2026-10-27. This information may be out of date; confirm on the official source. This document is the Fee Schedule, document RUB-DOC-01, version 1.0, effective 2026-10-01. Fees are quoted in Nigerian naira and shown with the ₦ symbol.

citation: Account Types and KYC Tiers, section 1 (Account types)
text:
Account Types and KYC Tiers > 1. Account types

Rubies offers two account types: savings and current. A savings account is for everyday saving and for receiving money such as a salary or a transfer. A current account is for customers who send and receive money more often, for example a small business. Both account types hold naira, receive transfers, and use a debit card. Both can be opened in the app after verification. The account type does not decide your KYC tier; the tier depends on the identity documents you provide. Fees for both account types are listed in the Fee Schedule.

citation: Account Types and KYC Tiers, section 2 (KYC tiers at a glance)
text:
Account Types and KYC Tiers > 2. KYC tiers at a glance

Rubies uses three KYC tiers: Tier 1, Tier 2 and Tier 3. A higher tier allows larger single transactions, larger daily totals, and a larger maximum balance. Tier 1 is the starting tier. Tier 2 needs both a BVN and a NIN. Tier 3 needs both, plus proof of address and a source of funds. As your tier rises, your limits rise. Upgrading is free. This section gives the overall picture; the next three sections explain each tier in full.

citation: Account Types and KYC Tiers, section 3 (Tier 1)
text:
Account Types and KYC Tiers > 3. Tier 1

Tier 1 is the entry tier at Rubies. To open a Tier 1 account, you provide a BVN or a NIN. Tier 1 allows a single transaction of up to ₦50,000. The daily limit is also ₦50,000, which means the total of your transactions in one day cannot pass ₦50,000. The maximum balance on a Tier 1 account is ₦300,000. If you need to send or hold more, you can upgrade to Tier 2. Tier 1 suits small everyday transactions and receiving small amounts.

citation: Account Types and KYC Tiers, section 4 (Tier 2)
text:
Account Types and KYC Tiers > 4. Tier 2

Tier 2 gives you more room. To move to Tier 2, you provide both a BVN and a NIN. Tier 2 allows a single transaction of up to ₦200,000. The daily limit is also ₦200,000. The maximum balance on a Tier 2 account is ₦500,000. Tier 2 is useful if you receive a salary or run a small business. If your balance reaches the cap, further credits are blocked until you upgrade. The steps to upgrade are explained later in this document.

citation: Account Types and KYC Tiers, section 5 (Tier 3)
text:
Account Types and KYC Tiers > 5. Tier 3

Tier 3 is the highest tier at Rubies. To reach Tier 3, you provide a BVN and a NIN, plus proof of address and a source of funds. Tier 3 allows a single transaction of up to ₦5,000,000. The daily limit is also ₦5,000,000. The maximum balance on a Tier 3 account is no limit, so you can hold as much as you need. Tier 3 suits customers with larger, regular money movements. Many customers stay on a lower tier until their needs grow.

citation: Account Types and KYC Tiers, section 6 (BVN and NIN requirements)
text:
Account Types and KYC Tiers > 6. BVN and NIN requirements

Rubies asks for identity documents to keep accounts safe and to meet Nigerian rules. A BVN is your Bank Verification Number. A NIN is your National Identification Number. For Tier 1, one of the two is enough. For Tier 2 and Tier 3, both are required. Since December 2023, Tier 2 and Tier 3 accounts need both a BVN and a NIN. This change applies to new upgrades. If you are unsure which documents you have, a chat agent can tell you.

citation: Account Types and KYC Tiers, section 7 (Upgrading to a higher tier)
text:
Account Types and KYC Tiers > 7. Upgrading to a higher tier

Upgrading your tier is free. You can start the upgrade in the app or with a chat agent. Rubies will ask for the documents the next tier needs. For Tier 2, that means both a BVN and a NIN. For Tier 3, that means both, plus proof of address and source of funds. Once your documents are checked, your new limits apply. Your balance stays the same during the upgrade. You can move from Tier 1 to Tier 2, or from Tier 2 to Tier 3.

section_heading: What happens when a limit is reached
citation: Account Types and KYC Tiers, section 8 (What happens when a limit is reached)
text:
Account Types and KYC Tiers > 8. What happens when a limit is reached

Limits protect you and meet regulatory rules. If a transfer is above your single transaction limit, Rubies declines it. If the transfer would push your daily total above your daily limit, Rubies also declines it. If a credit would push your balance above your maximum balance, Rubies blocks that credit. In all three cases, the fix is the same: upgrade to a higher tier. A chat agent will explain the limit that was reached and what the next tier allows.

citation: Account Types and KYC Tiers, section 9 (Documents for opening an account)
text:
Account Types and KYC Tiers > 9. Documents for opening an account

To open a Rubies account, you need a phone number and an identity document. The phone number is used for verification. For Tier 1, you provide a BVN or a NIN. For Tier 2, you provide both a BVN and a NIN. For Tier 3, you also provide proof of address and a source of funds. Proof of address is a recent document showing where you live. Source of funds explains where your money comes from. Keep your documents current.

text:
Account Types and KYC Tiers > 10. Sources and currency

citation: Transfers and Failed Transactions, section 1 (Types of transfer)
text:
Transfers and Failed Transactions > 1. Types of transfer

Rubies customers can send money in two main ways. A transfer to another Rubies account moves money between two Rubies customers. A transfer to another bank moves money out of Rubies through the NIP network. Each type has its own fee, described in the Fee Schedule. Every transfer gets a reference. The reference is how Rubies finds the transfer later. Keep the reference safe. You can send a transfer from the app or by asking a chat agent. The type of transfer affects the fee and how long the money takes.

citation: Transfers and Failed Transactions, section 2 (Transfer statuses)
text:
Transfers and Failed Transactions > 2. Transfer statuses

Every Rubies transfer has a status. Success means the money reached the beneficiary and the transfer is complete. Failed means the transfer did not go through; the money is returned to you. Pending means Rubies has accepted the request but the beneficiary bank has not yet confirmed it. Reversed means the transfer was undone and the money went back to the sender. A chat agent can read the current status for any transfer you own. The status can change while a transfer is being processed, so check again later if it is still pending.

citation: Transfers and Failed Transactions, section 3 (When a transfer fails)
text:
Transfers and Failed Transactions > 3. When a transfer fails

A transfer can fail for several reasons. The beneficiary bank may time out, the beneficiary account may be closed, or the details may be wrong. When a transfer fails, the money is not lost. For example, a ₦50,000 transfer may fail with the reason "Beneficiary bank timeout". Rubies shows the reason in plain words. Failed transfers do not reduce your balance. You can check the status yourself, or ask a chat agent. If a failed transfer caused a wrong charge, you can raise a dispute using the Disputes and Complaints Procedure.

citation: Transfers and Failed Transactions, section 4 (Automatic reversal timeline)
text:
Transfers and Failed Transactions > 4. Automatic reversal timeline

When a transfer fails, Rubies reverses the money automatically. The automatic reversal happens within 24 hours of the failure. You do not need to ask for it. The money goes back to the account it came from. If you do not see the reversal within 24 hours, contact a chat agent with the transaction reference. Rubies will check the transfer and confirm what happened. A failed transfer should never leave your balance lower than it was before. If it does, that is a problem to report straight away.

citation: Transfers and Failed Transactions, section 5 (Money debited but not received)
text:
Transfers and Failed Transactions > 5. Money debited but not received

Sometimes a transfer shows as pending. This means the money has left your account but the beneficiary bank has not confirmed it. For example, a ₦15,000 transfer may stay pending for a short time. Pending does not mean the money is gone. It means the transfer is still being processed. Rubies keeps checking with the other bank. If the transfer later succeeds, the beneficiary receives the money. If it fails, the money is reversed automatically within 24 hours. Check the status again after some time.

citation: Transfers and Failed Transactions, section 6 (Double debit)
text:
Transfers and Failed Transactions > 6. Double debit

A double debit happens when the same transfer is taken from your account twice. For example, a customer may be debited ₦25,000 twice for a single payment. A double debit is a wrongful debit. Rubies treats it as a serious problem. When you report it, Rubies reviews both entries and the transfer reference. If the second debit is wrong, Rubies reverses it. Double debit problems are resolved within 5 working days. Keep both references and the date ready when you report the problem.

section_heading: Information needed to report a problem
citation: Transfers and Failed Transactions, section 7 (Information needed to report a problem)
text:
Transfers and Failed Transactions > 7. Information needed to report a problem

To report a transfer problem, have four things ready. First, the transaction reference. A Rubies reference starts with the letters RUB, then a hyphen, two digits, a hyphen, and six digits. Second, the amount in naira. Third, the date of the transfer. Fourth, the beneficiary name and bank. These details let Rubies find the exact transfer. A chat agent may also ask for the phone number on your account. Never share your PIN, OTP, CVV or password; Rubies will never ask for them.

section_heading: How to check a transfer status with Rubies
citation: Transfers and Failed Transactions, section 8 (How to check a transfer status with Rubies)
text:
Transfers and Failed Transactions > 8. How to check a transfer status with Rubies

You can check a transfer status with a chat agent or by USSD. On USSD, dial *000# and follow the menu. A chat agent can read the status of any transfer you own, once you are verified. To verify, you give your phone number and a one-time code sent to you. The status is shown in plain words, such as success, failed, pending or reversed. If a transfer is still pending, check again later. Keep the reference so the check is quick.

text:
Transfers and Failed Transactions > 9. Sources and currency

section_heading: When to raise a dispute or complaint
citation: Disputes and Complaints Procedure, section 1 (When to raise a dispute or complaint)
text:
Disputes and Complaints Procedure > 1. When to raise a dispute or complaint

You can raise a dispute or complaint when something looks wrong with your money or your service. Common reasons are a failed transfer, a double debit, a wrong debit, a fee you did not expect, or a loan problem. A dispute is about a specific transaction. A complaint is a broader problem with the service. Rubies treats both seriously. Raise the issue as soon as you notice it, so the details are fresh. You can raise it with a chat agent, and you will be verified before anything is changed.

citation: Disputes and Complaints Procedure, section 2 (How to raise one)
text:
Disputes and Complaints Procedure > 2. How to raise one

To raise a dispute or complaint, Rubies first verifies you. You give the phone number on your account, and Rubies sends a one-time code. The code is a 6-digit number. It is valid for 300 seconds. You have 3 attempts to enter it correctly. After too many wrong attempts, the code is locked and you must request a new one. Once verified, your session lasts 15 minutes. During that time you can raise the dispute or complaint without verifying again. Rubies never asks for your PIN, OTP, CVV or password.

citation: Disputes and Complaints Procedure, section 3 (Disputing a transaction)
text:
Disputes and Complaints Procedure > 3. Disputing a transaction

When you dispute a transaction, Rubies does not log it straight away. Rubies first proposes the dispute and explains what will happen. Nothing changes until you say yes. When you agree, Rubies opens the dispute and returns a ticket number. The ticket number is your proof that the dispute is logged. Keep it safe. Only one open dispute can exist for the same transaction. If you try to dispute the same transaction twice, Rubies tells you it is already open.

citation: Disputes and Complaints Procedure, section 4 (What happens after)
text:
Disputes and Complaints Procedure > 4. What happens after

After you raise a dispute or complaint, Rubies acknowledges it within 24 hours. The acknowledgement confirms that Rubies has received the issue and gives you the ticket number again. Rubies then looks into the matter and keeps you updated. You do not need to repeat the issue. If Rubies needs more information, a chat agent will ask. The acknowledgement within 24 hours is a Rubies commitment. It is faster than the CBN guide, which expects a tracking number within 3 days.

citation: Disputes and Complaints Procedure, section 5 (Resolution timelines)
text:
Disputes and Complaints Procedure > 5. Resolution timelines

Rubies aims to resolve issues within clear timelines. A failed transfer, a double debit or a wrongful debit is resolved within 5 working days. A loan dispute or a fee dispute is resolved within 30 days. A general complaint is resolved within 14 days. A failed transfer is also reversed automatically within 24 hours, separate from the dispute. The timelines run from the day Rubies acknowledges the issue. If a timeline passes without resolution, you can escalate, as the next part of this procedure explains.

citation: Disputes and Complaints Procedure, section 6 (Escalation steps)
text:
Disputes and Complaints Procedure > 6. Escalation steps

If your issue is not resolved, you can escalate step by step. L1 is the chat agent ticket, which is where every issue starts. L2 is the Complaints Desk. You can reach the Complaints Desk at complaints@rubiesmfb.example or on 0700 000 0001. L3 is the Head of Customer Experience, at customercare.head@rubiesmfb.example. Each level reviews what the previous level did. Keep your ticket number and any messages ready when you escalate.

section_heading: Escalating to the CBN Consumer Protection Department
citation: Disputes and Complaints Procedure, section 7 (Escalating to the CBN Consumer Protection Department)
text:
Disputes and Complaints Procedure > 7. Escalating to the CBN Consumer Protection Department

If a timeline passes without resolution, you can escalate to the CBN Consumer Protection Department. Only escalate after the timeline above has passed. Bring evidence of your first complaint, such as the ticket number and the acknowledgement. The CBN address is cpd@cbn.gov.ng. Explain the issue, what Rubies did, and what is still unresolved. Keep copies of everything you send. Escalating to the CBN does not stop Rubies from resolving the issue; you can still accept a solution from Rubies.

section_heading: What to include in a complaint
citation: Disputes and Complaints Procedure, section 8 (What to include in a complaint)
text:
Disputes and Complaints Procedure > 8. What to include in a complaint

Include clear facts in your complaint. Give your ticket number, if you have one. Give the transaction reference, the amount in naira, and the date. A Rubies reference starts with the letters RUB, then a hyphen, two digits, a hyphen, and six digits. Describe what you expected and what happened. Say what outcome you want, such as a reversal or a refund. Keep your messages short and factual. Do not include your PIN, OTP, CVV or password. Rubies will never ask for them.

section_heading: Handing over to a human agent
citation: Disputes and Complaints Procedure, section 9 (Handing over to a human agent)
text:
Disputes and Complaints Procedure > 9. Handing over to a human agent

Some issues are handed over to a human agent. Rubies hands over when you ask for a human, when you are clearly upset, when a tool keeps failing, or when verification fails too many times. The human receives a short summary of the conversation, not the whole chat. The summary is capped at 1,000 characters and states the reason for the handover. This means the human can pick up quickly. You will be told when the handover happens and what to expect next.

citation: Disputes and Complaints Procedure, section 10 (Sources and currency)
text:
Disputes and Complaints Procedure > 10. Sources and currency

Rubies complaint timelines and escalation steps are guided by CBN rules. Source id: cbn_how_to_lodge_complaints. URL: https://www.cbn.gov.ng/FinInc/FinLit/How_Lodge_Complaints.pdf. Source id: cbn_consumer_protection_regulations_2_0. URL: https://www.cbn.gov.ng/Out/2024/CCD/EXPOSURE%20DRAFT%20REVISED%20CONSUMER%20PROTECTION%20REGULATIONS%202.0.pdf. citation: Cards, USSD and App Guide, section 1 (Rubies debit card)
text:
Cards, USSD and App Guide > 1. Rubies debit card

A Rubies debit card is a card linked to your account. You use it at ATMs, at POS terminals and online. A card has a status. Active means the card works and can be used. Blocked means the card is stopped and cannot be used. A card is blocked when you report it lost or stolen. Blocking is permanent until Rubies issues a replacement. You can see your card status in the app or by asking a chat agent. The card number is never shown in full in chat.

citation: Cards, USSD and App Guide, section 2 (Activating a new card)
text:
Cards, USSD and App Guide > 2. Activating a new card

When you receive a new Rubies debit card, it must be activated. You activate it in the app or with a chat agent. Rubies verifies you with your phone number and a one-time code before the card is activated. You then set your card PIN. Choose a PIN you can remember but that others cannot guess. Never write your PIN where someone can see it. Once activated, the card can be used at ATMs, POS terminals and online. Activation does not change your account balance.

citation: Cards, USSD and App Guide, section 3 (Lost, stolen or missing card)
text:
Cards, USSD and App Guide > 3. Lost, stolen or missing card

If your card is lost, stolen or missing, tell Rubies at once. Rubies verifies you with your phone number and a one-time code. Rubies then identifies the card by its last four digits. Rubies proposes the block and you must reply yes before it happens. The block takes effect immediately after you confirm. Next, request a replacement card. The replacement fee is ₦1,500 and the new card is ready in 5 working days. Report any transaction you do not recognise using the Disputes and Complaints Procedure.

section_heading: What a blocked card can and cannot do
citation: Cards, USSD and App Guide, section 4 (What a blocked card can and cannot do)
text:
Cards, USSD and App Guide > 4. What a blocked card can and cannot do

A blocked card cannot be used. It cannot be used at ATMs, at POS terminals or online. A blocked card cannot be unblocked; instead, Rubies issues a replacement card. Your account is not blocked. Money can still reach your account through transfers. You can still check your balance and use USSD and the app. The blocked card stays on your record as blocked. If you later find the card, tell a chat agent; it stays blocked for your safety.

citation: Cards, USSD and App Guide, section 5 (Keeping your PIN safe)
text:
Cards, USSD and App Guide > 5. Keeping your PIN safe

Your card PIN and your one-time code are private. Never share your PIN, CVV, OTP or password with anyone. Rubies will never ask for your PIN, OTP, CVV or password by chat, phone, SMS or email. If someone asks, it is a scam. Do not enter your PIN on any page opened from a message. A chat agent may ask you to enter your PIN only in the app's secure screen. Keep your phone locked. If you think someone knows your PIN, change it in the app.

citation: Cards, USSD and App Guide, section 6 (USSD banking)
text:
Cards, USSD and App Guide > 6. USSD banking

Rubies USSD banking works on any phone. Dial *000# to start. USSD can show your balance, send a mini statement, and start a transfer. USSD uses the same verification as the app: your phone number and a one-time code. USSD uses the same fees as the app. A balance enquiry costs ₦0 and a mini statement costs ₦0. A transfer fee depends on the amount, as listed in the Fee Schedule. If a session times out, dial again and verify afresh.

citation: Cards, USSD and App Guide, section 7 (The Rubies mobile app)
text:
Cards, USSD and App Guide > 7. The Rubies mobile app

The Rubies mobile app lets you manage your money. You log in with your phone number and a one-time code. If you forget your password, use the app's reset option; Rubies verifies you with a one-time code before any reset. In the app you can find your balance, your mini statement and your certified statement. A certified statement costs ₦1,000. The app never asks for your PIN by message. Keep the app updated for the latest safety fixes.

citation: Cards, USSD and App Guide, section 8 (Card and channel problems)
text:
Cards, USSD and App Guide > 8. Card and channel problems

Sometimes a card or a channel does not work. If your card is declined, check that it is active and that your balance is enough. If there is no network, try again later. If USSD does not respond, dial again. If the problem continues, contact the Complaints Desk at complaints@rubiesmfb.example or on 0700 000 0001. Tell them what you tried and what happened. For a wrong or double debit, use the Disputes and Complaints Procedure.

citation: Cards, USSD and App Guide, section 9 (Sources and currency)
text:
Cards, USSD and App Guide > 9. Sources and currency

This document is Rubies' own procedure. It does not cite an external regulation. Rubies card, USSD and app steps follow Rubies Microfinance Bank's internal rules. Date read: 2026-10-27. This information may be out of date; confirm on the official source. This document is Cards, USSD and App Guide, document RUB-DOC-05, version 1.0. All amounts are in Nigerian naira.

citation: Loan Products and Requirements, section 1 (Loan products)
text:
Loan Products and Requirements > 1. Loan products

Rubies offers two loan products: the Quick Salary Loan and the Small Business Loan. The Quick Salary Loan is for customers with regular salary inflow. The Small Business Loan is for customers who run a small business. Both are naira loans, repaid over a fixed tenor. Both use the same eligibility check and the same fees. You apply in the app or with a chat agent. A loan is only created after the eligibility check and after you accept the offer. This document explains the products, fees and requirements.

citation: Loan Products and Requirements, section 2 (Amounts and tenors)
text:
Loan Products and Requirements > 2. Amounts and tenors

Rubies loan tenors run from 3 to 12 months. You choose a tenor inside that range. The loan amount is not fixed; it depends on the eligibility check. The check looks at your account age, your average monthly inflow and any loan you already have. The largest amount Rubies will consider in an eligibility check is ₦500,000. If you ask for more than that, the check returns not eligible for the requested amount. The exact amount offered is shown only after the check.

citation: Loan Products and Requirements, section 3 (Loan fees)
text:
Loan Products and Requirements > 3. Loan fees

Rubies charges two fees on a loan. The management fee is 1% of the loan amount. The insurance fee is 0.5% of the loan amount. Both fees are charged upfront, before disbursement. For a ₦200,000 loan, the management fee is ₦2,000 and the insurance fee is ₦1,000, a total upfront cost of ₦3,000. Apart from these two fees, Rubies does not add hidden charges. The interest rate is not stated in this document; it is shown on your offer before you accept it.

citation: Loan Products and Requirements, section 4 (Eligibility requirements)
text:
Loan Products and Requirements > 4. Eligibility requirements

The eligibility check uses set requirements. Your account must be at least 30 days old. Your average monthly inflow must be at least ₦100,000. You must not already have an active loan. Your KYC tier must be Tier 1, Tier 2 or Tier 3; all three tiers are allowed. The requested amount must not exceed ₦500,000. The requested amount must not exceed your average monthly inflow multiplied by 3. You must meet every requirement to get an eligible result.

citation: Loan Products and Requirements, section 5 (How the eligibility check works)
text:
Loan Products and Requirements > 5. How the eligibility check works

The eligibility check is rule-based. It reads your account age, your average monthly inflow, any existing loan, your KYC tier and the amount you asked for. It then returns one of three results: eligible, not eligible, or needs review. Each result comes with a plain reason. The check is not a loan offer and it is not an approval. It only shows whether you would pass the rules today. A real offer can still be declined after the check.

citation: Loan Products and Requirements, section 6 (Documents and information needed)
text:
Loan Products and Requirements > 6. Documents and information needed

To apply for a Rubies loan, you need your phone number for verification. Depending on your KYC tier, you may need a BVN and a NIN; the Account Types and KYC Tiers document explains the documents for each tier. You need an open account with regular inflow, because the check reads your account history. No separate bank statement is needed for the check. A chat agent may ask what the loan is intended for. Keep your KYC documents current.

citation: Loan Products and Requirements, section 7 (Applying for NGN 200,000)
text:
Loan Products and Requirements > 7. Applying for NGN 200,000

If you ask for ₦200,000, the check would require the following. Your account must be at least 30 days old. Your average monthly inflow must be at least ₦100,000. You must not already have an active loan. Your KYC tier must be Tier 1, Tier 2 or Tier 3. The amount must not exceed ₦500,000, which ₦200,000 does not. The amount must not exceed your average monthly inflow multiplied by 3, so your monthly inflow must be at least one third of ₦200,000. Passing the check is not a promise of approval.

citation: Loan Products and Requirements, section 8 (Repayment and loan status)
text:
Loan Products and Requirements > 8. Repayment and loan status

If you have an active loan, you can see its status with a chat agent. Rubies shows the outstanding balance in naira and the next repayment date and amount. You repay the loan over the tenor you chose. Repaying on time keeps your account in good standing. If you think you will miss a repayment, contact a chat agent early. You can check your loan status at any time. The status shows whether the loan is active, completed or defaulted.

citation: Loan Products and Requirements, section 9 (Loan disputes and charges)
text:
Loan Products and Requirements > 9. Loan disputes and charges

If you disagree with a loan charge, you can dispute it. Rubies first proposes the dispute and you must say yes before it is logged. A loan dispute or a fee dispute is resolved within 30 days. A failed transfer or a wrongful debit follows a shorter timeline and is resolved within 5 working days. The full steps and escalation levels are in the Disputes and Complaints Procedure. Keep your ticket number once the dispute is logged.

citation: Loan Products and Requirements, section 10 (Sources and currency)
text:
Loan Products and Requirements > 10. Sources and currency

The Rubies loan timeline and the 30-day resolution window are guided by the CBN "How to Lodge a Complaint" guide. Source id: cbn_how_to_lodge_complaints. URL: https://www.cbn.gov.ng/FinInc/FinLit/How_Lodge_Complaints.pdf. Date read: 2026-10-27. This information may be out of date; confirm on the official source. This document is Loan Products and Requirements, document RUB-DOC-06, version 1.0. All amounts are in Nigerian naira.

section_heading: What Rubies will never ask you for
citation: Fraud and Security, section 1 (What Rubies will never ask you for)
text:
Fraud and Security > 1. What Rubies will never ask you for

Rubies will never ask you for any of these: full PIN, PIN, OTP, card CVV, full card number, password, BVN or NIN. This applies to chat, phone calls, SMS, email and social media. If anyone asks you for any of these, it is not Rubies. Do not reply and do not send anything. Report it to a chat agent straight away. Knowing this list is your best protection, so keep it in mind whenever someone contacts you and claims to be from Rubies.

citation: Fraud and Security, section 2 (Common scams)
text:
Fraud and Security > 2. Common scams

Fraudsters use the same tricks again and again. One trick is a fake alert or credit message saying you received money that you did not receive. Another is a fake "Rubies staff" call asking you to confirm your account. A SIM swap takes over your phone line so codes go to the fraudster. Phishing links look like real pages and ask you to log in. A fake loan fee asks you to pay before a loan is released. A fake reversal offer says a failed transfer will be reversed if you share details. Rubies never asks for money or secrets to release a loan or a reversal.

section_heading: Protecting your one-time code and PIN
citation: Fraud and Security, section 3 (Protecting your one-time code and PIN)
text:
Fraud and Security > 3. Protecting your one-time code and PIN

Your one-time code and your PIN are private. Never share your one-time code with anyone. Never share your PIN with anyone. Rubies sends a one-time code only to the phone number on your account. Enter it only in the app or on USSD. Do not read it out to a caller and do not enter it on a page opened from a message. If someone says they need your code to help you, that is a scam. Change your PIN in the app if you think someone has seen it.

section_heading: How to tell a real Rubies message from a fake one
citation: Fraud and Security, section 4 (How to tell a real Rubies message from a fake one)
text:
Fraud and Security > 4. How to tell a real Rubies message from a fake one

A real Rubies message comes only through official channels. These are the Rubies app, the USSD code *000#, and the Complaints Desk at complaints@rubiesmfb.example or on 0700 000 0001. A real message never asks for your PIN, one-time code, CVV, full card number, password, BVN or NIN. A real message never asks you to pay a fee to release money. If a message uses another channel or points to another link, treat it as fake and do not act on it.

section_heading: If you shared your details by mistake
citation: Fraud and Security, section 5 (If you shared your details by mistake)
text:
Fraud and Security > 5. If you shared your details by mistake

Act quickly if you shared details by mistake. First, block your card at once; blocking takes effect immediately after you confirm. Second, change your password in the app. Third, contact Rubies at the Complaints Desk email or phone and explain what happened. A chat agent will review recent activity with you. Report any transaction you do not recognise using the Disputes and Complaints Procedure. The sooner you act, the easier it is to limit the damage.

citation: Fraud and Security, section 6 (Reporting fraud)
text:
Fraud and Security > 6. Reporting fraud

Report fraud as soon as you notice it. Rubies acknowledges a fraud report within 24 hours. A wrongful debit is resolved within 5 working days. A failed transfer is reversed automatically within 24 hours, separately from the report. Give the transaction reference, the amount in naira and the date. The full steps are in the Disputes and Complaints Procedure. Keep your ticket number once the report is logged, and keep any messages or links you received as evidence.

section_heading: How the chat assistant verifies you
citation: Fraud and Security, section 7 (How the chat assistant verifies you)
text:
Fraud and Security > 7. How the chat assistant verifies you

The chat assistant verifies you before it shares account details. You give the phone number on your account, and Rubies sends a one-time code. The code is a 6-digit number. It is valid for 300 seconds. You have 3 attempts to enter it correctly. Once verified, your session lasts 15 minutes. The assistant never asks for your PIN. The assistant will not discuss another person's account, and it shows data only for the account it has just verified.

citation: General FAQ, section 1 (About Rubies)
text:
General FAQ > 1. About Rubies

Rubies Microfinance Bank serves customers with everyday banking. It offers savings and current accounts, transfers, debit cards, loans and a chat assistant. The chat assistant answers questions and can start actions such as a dispute or a card block. It also hands over to a human agent when that is needed. This General FAQ gives quick answers to common questions. The topic documents in this guide explain each area in full, and they are the better place to read for detail.

citation: General FAQ, section 2 (Accounts and tiers)
text:
General FAQ > 2. Accounts and tiers

**Q: What account types does Rubies offer?** A: Savings and current.
**Q: What tier do I start on?** A: Tier 1. Higher tiers allow larger limits.
**Q: What does Tier 2 need?** A: Both a BVN and a NIN.
**Q: What does Tier 3 add?** A: Proof of address and a source of funds.
**Q: What is the Tier 3 maximum balance?** A: No limit.

citation: General FAQ, section 3 (Fees)
text:
General FAQ > 3. Fees

**Q: What is the fee to send money to another bank?** A: It depends on the amount. Up to ₦5,000 costs ₦10. From ₦5,001 to ₦50,000 costs ₦25. Above ₦50,000 costs ₦53.75 including VAT.
**Q: What is the fee to send to another Rubies account?** A: ₦0.
**Q: What does an SMS alert cost?** A: ₦4 per SMS.
**Q: What does card replacement cost?** A: ₦1,500.
**Q: What does a balance enquiry cost?** A: ₦0.

citation: General FAQ, section 4 (Transfers)
text:
General FAQ > 4. Transfers

**Q: How long does a failed transfer take to reverse?** A: Within 24 hours, automatically.
**Q: What does pending mean?** A: The money has left your account but the other bank has not confirmed it yet.
**Q: How long does a double debit take to resolve?** A: Within 5 working days.
**Q: How do I check a transfer status?** A: Ask a chat agent, or dial *000# and follow the menu.

citation: General FAQ, section 5 (Cards)
text:
General FAQ > 5. Cards

**Q: What does a blocked card mean?** A: The card is stopped and cannot be used.
**Q: What should I do if my card is lost?** A: Tell Rubies at once. Rubies proposes a block and you reply yes before it happens.
**Q: When does a card block take effect?** A: Immediately after you confirm.
**Q: What does a replacement card cost and when is it ready?** A: ₦1,500, and it is ready in 5 working days.

citation: General FAQ, section 6 (Loans)
text:
General FAQ > 6. Loans

**Q: What loan products does Rubies offer?** A: The Quick Salary Loan and the Small Business Loan.
**Q: What tenors are available?** A: From 3 to 12 months.
**Q: What upfront fees apply?** A: A management fee of 1% and an insurance fee of 0.5%.
**Q: What are the fees on a ₦200,000 loan?** A: ₦2,000 management and ₦1,000 insurance.
**Q: How long does a loan dispute take?** A: It is resolved within 30 days.

citation: General FAQ, section 7 (Disputes and complaints)
text:
General FAQ > 7. Disputes and complaints

**Q: How do I raise a dispute?** A: Rubies proposes it and you must say yes before it is logged.
**Q: How long until you acknowledge a complaint?** A: Within 24 hours.
**Q: How long does a general complaint take?** A: It is resolved within 14 days.
**Q: How do I reach the Complaints Desk?** A: At complaints@rubiesmfb.example or on 0700 000 0001.
**Q: How do I escalate?** A: Start at L1, then the Complaints Desk, then the Head of Customer Experience, and the CBN if the timeline passes.

citation: General FAQ, section 8 (Talking to a human agent)
text:
General FAQ > 8. Talking to a human agent

**Q: When does the assistant hand over to a human?** A: When you ask for a human, when you are upset, when a tool keeps failing, or when verification fails too many times.
**Q: Do I have to repeat everything?** A: No. The human receives a short summary of the chat.
**Q: How long is that summary?** A: It is capped at 1,000 characters.
**Q: Where do I start if I need help?** A: Ask the chat assistant, or email the Complaints Desk.

citation: General FAQ, section 9 (Security)
text:
General FAQ > 9. Security

**Q: Will Rubies ever ask for my PIN?** A: Never. Rubies will never ask for your PIN, OTP, CVV or password.
**Q: How do I spot a fake message?** A: A real message never asks for secrets and never asks you to pay to release money.
**Q: What should I do if I shared details by mistake?** A: Block your card at once, change your password, and contact Rubies.
